correctness.rationale: The six coordinate edges and three pairing lines exhaust the lines: on any other proposed line the four coordinate linear forms are nonzero; the identity that the sum of their reciprocals vanishes forces cancellation of the poles in two proportional pairs, each with opposite forms. Otherwise the parametrization would be constant. Distinct pairing-line intersections are distinct in characteristic >3; coordinate-vertex germs of the reduced divisor are three independent coordinate axes in an affine chart, and all remaining intersections are ordinary two-axis germs. Thus the normalization is nine rational components with seminormal gluing. There are 4 three-branch and 9 two-branch points. Branch multipliers modulo rescalings on components and common rescalings at each singular point are the whole connected Picard group: for these germs the unit quotient sees only branch constants, so there is no additive part. Dualizing this torus quotient gives the oriented integral graph kernel, equivariantly, of rank 30−22+1=9. A spanning-tree cycle basis is integral by its unit chord coordinates. Independently enumerating the coordinate line sets and their intersections over F5 and applying the five permutations to the actual points and branches reproduces all orbit rows. The determinant on the graph kernel is (t−1) times the branch permutation determinant divided by the component and point determinants; this reproduces all five characteristic polynomials. The coordinate incidence argument, not the sample characteristic, supplies the general profiles. Counting rational normalization points separately on every fixed line and replacing the fixed preimages over each fixed singular point gives the extension-count identity; its exponential gives the orbit product. A rational torus point is a homomorphism from the lattice to the algebraic closure's units satisfying h(Fx)=h(x)^q; the resulting finite Hom of the displayed cokernel has the same abstract invariant factors since det(qI−F) is prime to the characteristic. This proves the group formula and the order rows without inferring Smith factors from an isogeny.
residual_risks: No frozen checker executed. The independent finite enumeration checks incidence and orbit arithmetic, not geometric local rings in all characteristics or an independently reduced symbolic Smith form. The general proof verifies the claimed presentation, not separate symbolic invariant factors.

evidence: Write v,e,m for fixed coordinate vertices, unordered pairs and matchings. Using the prior inversion, the full surface count is q²+q+1+q(e−v): subtract the union of four lines in the trace plane and add the six coordinate edges; the common ordered endpoint-incidence terms cancel. Subtracting the prior open counts recovers each divisor row, also for powers of Frobenius. Equivalently the divisor count is q(e+m)+v+2m−b−m(m−1) with b the fixed endpoint incidence count in that proof.

The prior complement zeta functions, or their fixed-point coefficients together with normalization, already determine the rational cycle traces and hence the order values. They do not determine the integral Picard lattice or its finite group merely from those numerical spectra.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The numerical arithmetic is credited as a consequence, not treated as independent novelty. An integral cycle model can be transported from the prior seven-line incidence via the graph contraction, but requires the additional comparison and the proof that the actual Cayley gluing yields the whole Picard torus; the prior numerical invariant is not an integral Picard result.

originality.rationale: Credit the nine lines and five twists as known, and the numerical divisor point counts, zeta functions and rational cycle spectra as recoverable from the prior line-free arithmetic and its proof. What remains distinct is the identification of the connected Picard scheme of the singular Cayley line union as a torus with an exact integral S4-cycle lattice, its descent, and the concrete finite-group presentations. The closest indexed method match treats a different genus-15 curve; the geometric Hilbert-scheme and surface Picard references do not identify this invariant.
residual_risks: Targeted literature comparison is bounded; it cannot rule out a differently indexed treatment of the integral comparison with the plane arrangement. The exact catalogue open arithmetic overlap is an implication, not a claim about priority of unpublished derivations.

value.rationale: The reduced union of all geometric lines is a canonical boundary of this singular cubic. Correctly distinguishing its four three-axis gluings from planar ordinary triples determines whether its connected Picard scheme has any additive contribution. A concrete integral equivariant lattice and finite presentation allow exact descent and finite-group calculations not licensed by rational zeta spectra alone. This is useful for comparing degenerations and twists even though independent novelty is not assigned to the point counts and symbolic Smith factors are not asserted.
residual_risks: The exact group is presented by a matrix, not simplified into cyclic factors for all q; the value lies in integral Picard structure, not just the numerical table.
